rationale: The working diagnosis identifies a real release-quality problem and strong founder fit but finds no demonstrated repeat demand, no initial moat, a low adjacent audit price anchor, and dependence on unproven private-data rights. The redesign applies the evaluator's highest-value change by constraining the offer to one frequent, evidence-supported failure mode—motion-induced PPG error—sold as an up-front gate for each release version. It tests CRO and regulatory-consultant introductions without claiming commitments, permits compounding only from contractually allowed derived failure features, and postpones the broad benchmark, subscription, proprietary collection, and regulatory-grade work. This preserves the opportunity's defensible identity as a neutral held-out wearable-signal decision gate while materially changing its scope, paid event, distribution, capital sequence, margin assumptions, and repeat economics. All pricing, repeat purchase, channel performance, decision impact, and reuse rights remain explicitly unvalidated.
